*Last updated: 2026-05-03 — Dual-domain architecture destinations documented per DEC-20260503-A: *[*strale.io*](http://strale.io)* (product website, *-Assurance family), [strale.dev](http://strale.dev) (agent capabilities API, passive surface), [api.strale.io](http://api.strale.io) (production API endpoint, unified backend). Brand identity differentiation per DEC-20260503-A: [strale.io](http://strale.io) light/professional/SaaS-trust-vertical; [strale.dev](http://strale.dev) dark/developer/breadth. Strale-owned destinations described in narrative below; not added as rows to the embedded Distribution Surfaces DB because that DB's 9 categories all describe third-party listing surfaces and don't fit own-domain destinations (CC judgment, see Session 3B Journal entry). Prior: 2026-04-27. First version written 2026-04-08 as part of the April 2026 cleanup; subsequent edits are inline.\*
**A distribution surface is any place where an agent, a developer, or an LLM can discover Strale without Strale having to run paid acquisition. The strategy is to be listed on every surface the target audience might look at, so that finding Strale doesn't require knowing Strale exists.**
The database at the bottom of this page is the single source of truth for every distribution surface. 42 surfaces across 9 categories. Add a row when a new surface is identified. Update the Status and Last verified date the same day anything changes. Never store surface status anywhere else — not in session logs, not in memory, not in Journal entries.
**What this database does NOT track:** individual blog posts, social media posts, Stack Overflow answers, or other ongoing content output. Content is produced continuously and would flood the registry. Content lives on the Social media shelf page.
# Where the surfaces drive traffic to (the destinations)
Per DEC-20260503-A, Strale operates two front-door surfaces under one company. These are the destinations the third-party distribution surfaces in the database below drive traffic to:
- [**strale.io**](http://strale.io) — the *-Assurance product family home (Counterparty Assurance, Web3 Assurance, future *-Assurance products). Light/professional/SaaS-trust-vertical brand. Active marketing investment concentrated here. Conversion-focused.
- [**strale.dev**](http://strale.dev) — the agent capabilities API. Atomic capabilities at per-call prices, surfaced via MCP / x402 / Stripe pre-paid / MPP / Stripe Link for Agents. Dark-mode developer identity, breadth-of-capability framing, monospace accents. Passive surface — no active marketing investment.
- [**api.strale.io**](http://api.strale.io) — the unified production API endpoint. Same backend serves both surfaces; same authentication, billing, audit infrastructure, `source_health` substrate.
Cross-link in footers only between [strale.io](http://strale.io) and [strale.dev](http://strale.dev), not in primary nav. Visitors arriving for one surface should not be diverted to the other unless they go looking.
Each third-party distribution surface in the database below drives traffic to one of these two front doors, depending on the audience the surface reaches. Agent-builder discovery (MCP registries, x402 facilitators, package registries, framework docs) routes to [strale.dev](http://strale.dev). Buyer discovery (content marketing, search, peer recommendation, eventually paid) routes to [strale.io](http://strale.io). LLM-discoverability assets feed both — [strale.dev](http://strale.dev) for capability-level recommendations, [strale.io](http://strale.io) for product-level recommendations.
# Why distribution surfaces matter more than paid acquisition
The audience Strale needs to reach is tiny, technical, and scattered. A developer looking for a sanctions-screening capability isn't on Facebook. They're searching MCP registries, reading GitHub awesome-lists, asking Cursor to recommend a tool, or hitting an LLM with "how do I verify a Swedish company programmatically." The goal is that Strale shows up in all of those places — without having to pay for the privilege each time.
This compounds. Every surface Strale is listed on increases the chance of showing up in the next surface: an LLM recommending Strale is more likely if Strale is in Context7 and has an llms.txt and is in the MCP Registry, because all three independently feed LLM training and retrieval. The surfaces reinforce each other.
# The nine categories
**MCP registries** — directories of Model Context Protocol servers. An agent calling an MCP-compatible tool discovers Strale here. All four major registries are live: Official MCP Registry (Linux Foundation), Glama (all A scores), Smithery, [mcp.so](http://mcp.so).
**MCP gateways** — runtime infrastructure that routes agent tool calls. Unlike registries, gateways are *runtime* — agents connected to a gateway discover Strale automatically, zero developer action required. Highest-leverage zero-touch acquisition surface. Four PRs pending (Docker, agentic-community, IBM Context Forge, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore).
**Awesome lists** — curated GitHub repositories of MCP servers, agent skills, and AI tools. Three pending, one merged (xpaysh/awesome-x402 — first awesome-list acceptance).
**Skill marketplaces** — platforms where end users browse and install agent skills. RapidAPI Hub is live. n8n Creator Portal pending verification. LobeHub, Anthropic, Salesforce AgentExchange still awaiting.
**Package registries** — npm and PyPI packages that make Strale easy to install. 14 packages total. SDKs (straleio npm \~321 monthly downloads, PyPI \~400), MCP server, six framework plugins (LangChain, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents, Google ADK, Pydantic AI, Semantic Kernel), two fallback packages, n8n node (\~102 weekly), scaffold CLI. All live except Activepieces piece (pending).
**Protocol ecosystem** — x402 and A2A. All capabilities and solutions available as x402 endpoints (DB-driven, adding a new endpoint is one SQL update). The x402.json manifest, A2A agent card, and x402 Bazaar protocol extension are all live. x402scan live (358 paid endpoints indexed 2026-04-27). x402-foundation partners PR pending.
**LLM discoverability** — every place an LLM might look when a developer asks it "how do I verify a Swedish company programmatically." llms.txt, robots.txt allowing all AI crawlers, optimised MCP tool descriptions, a [CLAUDE.md](http://CLAUDE.md) snippet, Context7 library index (113,964 tokens indexed, Trust Score 4), IDE rules for Cursor and Windsurf, 30 GitHub Gists. All live. This category is structurally complete.
**IDE rules collections** — community GitHub repos collecting Cursor and Windsurf rules. If a developer's IDE recommends Strale because the rules mention it, that's high-intent discovery — the developer is mid-task. Three pending PRs.
**Framework docs** — official documentation of agent frameworks (Pydantic AI, LangChain). Appearing in a framework's integration docs is the single highest-value surface because it's authoritative and cited by the LLMs those frameworks ship with.
**Content & SEO** — blog posts, social media, Stack Overflow. Two [Dev.to](http://Dev.to) posts live, two in draft. X active. LinkedIn deferred. Stack Overflow paused after a moderator warning for promotional posting. The lowest-converting category today.
# What's working and what isn't
**Working:**
- **The free-tier front door is generating more actual usage than all other surfaces combined.** 744 calls from 84 anonymous IPs in 30 days against five free utilities. Expanding this is the highest-priority discovery work on the Build Plan.
- **Package registries and protocol ecosystem** are all live and generating real traffic.
- **LLM discoverability infrastructure is complete.** Every piece that makes Strale recommendable by an LLM is in place, including Context7 indexing at Trust Score 4.
- **First awesome-list acceptance:** xpaysh/awesome-x402 merged 2026-04-03.
- **x402scan indexing live (358/358 endpoints)** as of 2026-04-27 after a four-commit fix in Strale's gateway: spec-compliant `/.well-known/x402` fan-out, paid-route `x-payment-info` annotations in `/openapi.json`, dropping the v1 `Payment-Required` header that confused agentcash's v2-only decoder, and excluding free-tier (\$0) capabilities from paid discovery. New paid capabilities propagate automatically via the same DB-backed cache.
**Not working or stalled:**
- **Broadcast content is near-zero conversion.** [Dev.to](http://Dev.to) articles (2 published) have produced no measurable traffic signal. X is active but isn't driving signups. The pattern is consistent with the broader principle that broadcast content has near-zero conversion without social proof — direct 1:1 outreach to developers with the specific problem is higher leverage.
- **Stack Overflow is paused.** First canonical answer got a moderator warning. Account needs 50+ organic rep before further Strale-related posts. 20 drafts sit ready.
- **LinkedIn isn't set up.** Deferred indefinitely.
- **ClawHub agent-skills repo returned 404.** Submission route is dead.
**Pending maintainer review:** 17+ PRs sitting across MCP gateways, awesome-lists, framework docs, and IDE rules collections. All CI green, all awaiting human maintainer action. The pattern is that getting CI green is the easy part; getting a human to merge is the bottleneck.
# The operating principle
**The database is the single source of truth for status.** Every surface Strale is listed on, submitted to, or trying to get exposure through has one row. When the status changes, the row is updated the same day. Before any action on a surface, the row is read first to confirm the action is an improvement over what currently exists.
**Any session that touches a distribution surface ends with updating the corresponding row.** This is the rule that keeps the database useful. The failure mode is work happening (a PR gets merged, a submission gets accepted) without the database reflecting it, so the next session acts on stale information and duplicates effort or misses a follow-up.
**The database is a working document, not a presentation.** It has stalled PRs sitting for weeks and statuses like "Blocked" or "Paused." That's correct — it reflects reality.
